title: Aston Martin DBX GT tanıtıldı: Lüks ve konfora odaklanan yeni super-SUV
summary: Aston Martin, DBX ailesine konforu ve sessizliği ön plana çıkaran yeni DBX GT modelini ekledi. Güçlü V8 motorunu koruyan araç, yılın son çeyreğinde yollarda olacak.
body:
Aston Martin, performans odaklı lüks SUV ailesini genişleterek konforu ve şıklığı ön plana çıkaran 2027 model Aston Martin DBX GT aracını tanıttı. Motor1 ve Car and Driver'ın aktardığına göre yeni model, markanın yüksek performansından ödün vermeden daha sakin ve rahat bir sürüş deneyimi sunmayı hedefliyor. Araç, DBX S modeliyle birlikte satışa sunulurken, daha önceki DBX 707 ise üretimden kalkıyor.

## Konfor odaklı tasarım ve yenilenen iç mekan

Motor1'in haberine göre DBX GT, dışarıda daha zarif bir görünüm sunan yeni çift çıtalı ön panjur ve 22 inçlik dövme jantlarla geliyor. Kabin içinde ise hem ön hem de arka koltuklar ekstra dolgu malzemesi ve hafızalı sünger katmanıyla yeniden tasarlandı. Car and Driver'ın raporuna göre Aston Martin, kapılara, tekerlek yuvalarına ve arka camlara eklediği ses yalıtımı malzemeleriyle kabin içindeki gürültüyü azaltarak yolcuların sohbet etmesini kolaylaştıran akustik iyileştirmeler de yaptı. Araca standart olarak panoramik cam tavan eşlik ediyor.

## Güçlü motor ve süspansiyon detayları

Kaputun altında çift turbo beslemeli 4.0 litrelik V8 motoru taşımaya devam eden lüks SUV, Motor1 verilerine göre **717 beygir** güç ve 664 libre-fit tork üretiyor. 0-60 mil/s hızlanmasını 3,1 saniyede tamamlayan ve 193 mil/s son hıza ulaşabilen araç, S modeliyle aynı performans değerlerini paylaşıyor. Buna karşın GT versiyonunda süspansiyon sönümleyicileri, şanzıman geçişleri ve gaz tepkileri daha pürüzsüz ve konforlu bir sürüş için özel olarak yeniden kalibre edildi.

**Neden önemli?** Aston Martin, performans SUV segmentinde saf güç ile günlük kullanım konforunu dengelemek isteyen kullanıcılar için yeni bir seçenek sunuyor. İlk teslimatların 2026'nın son çeyreğinde başlaması beklenirken, fiyat bilgisi henüz paylaşılmadı.

source_texts.title: Aston Martin's New DBX Shows Its Softer Side
source_texts.summary: The 2027 DBX GT gets a more comfortable ride, a quieter cabin, and upgraded seats without giving up the twin-turbo V8’s 717 horsepower.
source_texts.text:
Aston Martin's New DBX Shows Its Softer Side
The 2027 DBX GT gets a more comfortable ride, a quieter cabin, and upgraded seats without giving up the twin-turbo V8’s 717 horsepower.
The Aston Martin DBX is a performance SUV through and through. It has sharp styling, a sport-tuned suspension, and a whole lot of horsepower no matter which version you choose. But for buyers who want something a little more comfortable for everyday driving, Aston Martin now has an answer.
Meet the DBX GT, the slightly softer side of Aston Martin’s super SUV. It gets a series of changes to the exterior, interior, and suspension aimed at making the DBX more comfortable. The good news is, it doesn’t give up the performance that makes this SUV so special; it still packs a powerful twin-turbo V8.
2027 Aston Martin DBX GT
The DBX GT gets a handful of visual changes for a more elegant look. The biggest change is the new double-vaned grille, which is available in either a bright or dark finish. The split metal vanes extend into the outer vents and incorporate the daytime running lights, giving the front end a wider appearance.
There’s also a new two-piece metal side strake with contrasting polished and satin finishes. Aston Martin says the design takes inspiration from traditional watchmaking. The lower front bumper, side sills, and rear diffuser are finished in body color, giving the GT a cleaner appearance.
The GT rides on new 22-inch forged wheels with a Satin Titanium diamond-turned finish and all-season tires as standard. Aston Martin says the combination was chosen specifically to improve ride comfort and reduce road noise. Buyers looking for a sportier setup can step up to 23-inch wheels with either Pirelli P Zero summer tires or Scorpion Zero all-season tires.
Around back, the four exhaust outlets are arranged horizontally in pairs, with polished outer sections and satin-anodized inner sections.
The biggest changes are inside. Aston Martin has redesigned both the front and rear seats with additional cushioning, revised bolstering, and new contours focused on comfort. There’s also a 10.0-millimeter-thick layer of memory foam built into the seat cushions. Cushy.
The rear seats get individually sculpted seating positions with extended headrests and bolsters, although the DBX GT remains a five-seater. A panoramic glass roof is standard, bringing more light into the rear cabin.
Aston Martin has redesigned both the front and rear seats with additional cushioning, revised bolstering, and new contours focused on comfort.
Aston Martin also offers GT-specific upholstery combinations in monotone, duotone, and tritone configurations. The cabin uses semi-aniline leather, deep-pile carpeting, intricate quilting, perforations, and bespoke embroidery throughout.
Noise isolation has received attention, too. Aston Martin added sound-deadening material to the doors, wheel arches, and rear cargo area, while acoustic laminated glass is used for the rear side windows.
The company claims those changes improve the vehicle’s "Articulation Index" by 13 percent. That’s an industry measurement of how easily occupants can carry on a conversation while the vehicle is moving.
For all the focus on comfort, Aston Martin hasn’t softened the DBX GT where it matters most: the powertrain. It uses the same twin-turbocharged 4.0-liter V8 as the DBX S. And the specs are just as impressive:
- 717 HP / 664 LB-FT
- 0-60 MPH: 3.1 Seconds
- Top Speed: 193 MPH
The powertrain has been recalibrated slightly to make the GT feel more effortless. Throttle response has been tuned for more precise control, while the nine-speed wet-clutch automatic transmission gets revised shift calibration for smoother operation.
The DBX GT also gets the same carbon-ceramic brakes as the DBX S, measuring 420 millimeters up front and 390 mm at the rear. A quicker steering ratio carries over as well, giving the SUV sharper responses.
The suspension gets its own changes, too. The GT has a unique damper calibration and internal damper valves designed to better absorb small, high-frequency impacts such as rough pavement and rumble strips without giving up body control.
The DBX GT joins an already growing DBX lineup, giving buyers another option between outright performance and everyday comfort. Aston Martin hasn’t announced pricing yet. The DBX S starts at $291,200, so expect the GT to land somewhere in that neighborhood.
First deliveries are expected in the fourth quarter of 2026.

source_texts.title: 2027 Aston Martin DBX GT Is a More Elegant Spin on the Super SUV
source_texts.summary: The DBX GT has the same 717 horsepower as the DBX S, but gains a retuned suspension and more ornamental interior upholstery.
source_texts.text:
- Aston Martin has revealed the 2027 DBX GT, a more refined take on its super-SUV that will sit alongside the sportier DBX S.
- The DBX GT has the same 717-hp twin-turbo V-8, but the suspension and transmission have been retuned with a focus on comfort.
- Inside, the seats get new upholstery, with eye-catching stitching that runs along the side of the headrests.
Aston Martin is expanding the DBX lineup as its super-SUV enters its seventh year. After adding the DBX S for the 2026 model year, 2027 sees the introduction of the new DBX GT, which brings the same 717 horsepower as the DBX S but in a less aggressive package focused more on luxury and comfort.
The DBX GT has cleaner styling than its racy S counterpart, with the wide grille trading mesh for a series of horizontal bars, offered in bright and dark finishes. These lines reappear next to the horizontal LED daytime running lights at the outer edges of the bumper, while the lower grille opening skips the red trim for a more elegant look.
The two-piece metal side strake in the front fender wears a more graceful polished and satin dual finish, and the lower front bumper, side sills, and rear diffuser are all painted body color, instead of black as on the DBX S. The GT also rides on new 22-inch wheels with a Satin Titanium finish, wrapped in Pirelli Scorpion Zero all-season tires as standard, although a sportier 23-inch wheel and Pirelli P-Zero summer tire package is available. There are also new quad exhaust pipes that sit side by side instead of atop each other, while a unique exhaust tune provides a “cleaner, richer tone,” Aston Martin says.
Inside, Aston Martin focused on making the DBX feel even fancier via ornate new embroidery on the seats. This new stitching climbs up the side of the seats, framing the shoulder pads and headrest. The front and rear seats also gain extra cushioning, with a new 0.4-inch-thick memory foam layer added in. In the rear, the two outboard seats look more distinctly like separate seats thanks to more pronounced bolstering, while the middle seat gets upholstered in a different color.
Aston Martin also fitted more opulent interior trim pieces, such as the anodized metal drive mode dial, while deep pile floor mats round out the decadent cabin. Aston Martin also says it reduced cabin noise through improvements to the body structure and added sound-deadening material in the door panels and wheel arches, as well as acoustic laminated rear side glass. The DBX GT also gets a standard panoramic glass roof.
Under the hood sits the twin-turbocharged 4.0-liter V-8, which cranks out the same 717 horsepower and 664 pound-feet of torque as the DBX S. Aston Martin says the GT will match the S with a 3.1-second sprint to 60 mph and a 193-mph top speed. Stopping is handled by carbon-ceramic brakes with 16.5-inch discs up front and 15.4-inch discs at the rear.
Still, the DBX GT gets a unique suspension setup, with reworked dampers that help absorb bumps on rough roads while still providing body control when driving fast. Aston Martin also says it revised the throttle pedal feel for improved precision, and the nine-speed automatic gearbox has been retuned for smoother-feeling shifts. A new transmission mount bushing also aims to better control the movement of the transmission relative to the body, while two new longitudinal dampers have been added between the body and rear subframe.
The DBX GT will start reaching customers in the fourth quarter of this year. The GT will sit alongside the DBX S in the lineup for 2027, with the DBX 707 going the way of the dodo. Aston Martin has yet to divulge pricing, but we expect the DBX GT to start at around $290,000.
